title: My Soul, Repeat His Praise
description: My Soul, Repeat His Praise in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 103, part 4, headed “Abounding compassion of God; or, Mercy in the midst of judgment”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My soul, re-peat his praise Whose mer-cies are so great, Whose an-ger is so slow to rise, So rea-dy to a-bate.

lines: Whose anger is so slow to rise,
And when his strokes are felt,
His strokes are fewer than our crimes,
High as the heavens are rais'd
So far the riches of his grace
Far as the east is from the west,
To those that fear his Name,
Is such as tender parents feel;
He knows we are but dust,
His anger, like a rising wind,
Can send us swift to death.
Our days are as the grass,
If one sharp blast sweep o'er the field,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
